I figure things out for a living.

Sometimes it's AI.

Sometimes it's how to run a company without becoming the bottleneck.

Sometimes it's which tool is actually worth paying for, what to wear somewhere, how to plan something faster, or why the thing everyone on the internet is recommending is absolutely not worth it.

I test a lot.
I build a lot.
I ask way too many questions.

And when I find something genuinely useful, I put it here.

Welcome to AskSarah.

No 47-page ebook before you get the answer.
No pretending every product is life-changing.
No list of "10 AI tools you need" written by someone who hasn't used nine of them.

Just the things I use, build, recommend and would send to a friend.

What are you trying to figure out?

01 Skills

I got tired of explaining the same thing to AI over and over again.

So I started building Skills.

A prompt tells AI what you want right now.
A Skill teaches it how you want something done repeatedly.

These are the actual Skills I'm building and using for work, decisions, meetings, research, planning and everyday life.

Some are free.
Some took enough work that I'm charging you for them. 🙂

Browse the Skills →

02 Sarah's Stack

There is an absurd amount of software in my life.

Most of it does not survive.
This is what did.

AI tools. Work tools. Creator tools. Tech. Travel. Fitness. Beauty. Things on my desk. Things permanently living in my suitcase.

For every one, I'll tell you:

  • what I actually use it for
  • what I don't use it for
  • whether I pay for it
  • whether I think you should
  • what I would use instead if I stopped using it

If it's here, I've actually used it.

See my stack →

03 Shortcuts

These exist because I don't want to read a 2,000-word article when I have a problem.

I want someone to tell me what to do.

So these are the shortcuts.

How I prep for a difficult conversation.
How I turn a brain dump into an actual plan.
How I use AI before an important meeting.
How I figure out what to pack.
How I make a decision when I've researched it to death and somehow know less than when I started.

Little problems. Useful answers.

Give me a shortcut →

04 Systems

Some things need more than a shortcut.

These are the systems I've built because I needed them myself.

How I manage my week.
How I decide what only I should be doing.
How I use AI without creating more work for myself.
How I stop ideas from living in 14 tabs, three Notes files, a Slack message to myself and the notebook I can't find.

They aren't productivity theater.
They're meant to actually be used.

What I'm using AI for right now

I don't need AI to write me another blog post.

I need it to help me think.

Make a decision.
Prepare for a conversation.
Research something I don't have six hours to research.
Organize the thought currently ricocheting around my brain.
Teach me something.
Challenge me when I'm convinced I'm right.
Plan something.
Find the thing I forgot.
Turn chaos into something I can actually act on.

I'm building a running list of the ways I'm using AI in real life.

Not hypothetical use cases.
Actual ones.

The rule

If I wouldn't use it, I won't put it here.

If I wouldn't send it to a friend, I won't recommend it.

If something is sponsored or I make money when you buy it, I'll tell you.

And if I change my mind about something?
I'll tell you that too.

The internet has enough "ultimate guides."
I'd rather just help you figure something out.
